title: Critique and Thirty Improvements
excerpt: B"H Critique and Thirty Improvements 1. Do not mistake more outlines for realism; add planes, joints, overlap, and material cues. 2. Keep neutral identity separate from acting. 3. Prevent facial detail from becoming noise at 180×300. 4. Give ears and jaw different visibility by view. 5. Preserve eye readability during
searchText: b"h critique and thirty improvements 1. do not mistake more outlines for realism; add planes, joints, overlap, and material cues. 2. keep neutral identity separate from acting. 3. prevent facial detail from becoming noise at 180×300. 4. give ears and jaw different visibility by view. 5. preserve eye readability during extreme close ups and profiles. 6. make lips change clearly across visemes. 7. use elbows so gestures do not resemble rubber lines. 8. use knees so running and crouching have believable weight. 9. plant feet during stops and catches. 10. keep crossed arms and pocket contact locked. 11. attach carried props to the correct wrist side. 12. separate world objects from hand props. 13. use object materials: ceramic, metal, paper, glass, plastic, fabric, wood. 14. add object shadows and highlights. 15. give the office three depth layers. 16. let camera parallax affect world objects consistently. 17. make text bubbles point toward the speaker. 18. move bubbles away from faces and title safe regions. 19. wrap dialogue instead of shrinking it into illegibility. 20. keep every dialogue line within its authored timing. 21. use insert shots for mug, machine display, spoon, and printer output. 22. use an overhead shot to make the mug negotiation spatially clear. 23. use a dutch angle only at the machine malfunction. 24. use slow push and whip pan motion for escalation. 25. use a stable final group tableau for the punchline. 26. ensure objects persist in the source project and package. 27. ensure preview and final export use identical evaluated object state. 28. add tests that compare object hashes across action phases. 29. add tests for jointed limb geometry and anchored bubble placement. 30. reject completion if any proof frame is blank, clipped, symbolically crude, or visually repetitive. revised insight the prior short proved completeness, but this pass must prove cinematic density. the central improvement is not merely a different script; it is a reusable production layer where believable bodies and constructed objects share one camera, one timeline, one persistence contract, and one export path.

searchText: b"h delta planned versus actual the plan called for a much more realistic character renderer, realistic office objects, anchored bubbles, dense action, broad camera language, and a new one minute film. all planned systems were implemented. additional defects discovered and closed 1. the original arm path connected shoulder directly to wrist. jointed elbow geometry was added. 2. the original leg path connected hip directly to foot. jointed knee geometry and planted/crouched poses were added. 3. the office environment was a generic interior. a constructed three layer office set was added. 4. props were largely symbolic. material specific object painters and deterministic motion were added. 5. dialogue used full width banners. speaker anchored bubbles with tails and safe layout were added. 6. two authored camera move labels were not supported by the real motion library. the shot file was completely rewritten to use pursuit, crane, crash zoom, handheld, whip pan, slow push, pull back, and locked vocabulary. 7. the first head scale court sampled the closing title card. the court was rewritten to inspect rivky's actual 57.5 second reaction frame. 8. tunnel job receipts repeatedly vanished after transport restarts. restart proof repository side verification logs and exit files were created. 9. early exporter hashes were captured before artifact finalization. current media, preview, plan, and exporter manifest hashes were remeasured and proven identical. no unresolved delta remains.
